name: Burger Chef
closureReason: The chain was sold, and most locations were converted to Hardee's or other brands.
history: Burger Chef grew into a major hamburger chain and became known for family-oriented meals and bundled burger, fries, and drink offerings.
sourceNote: Historical sample compiled from public reference material; verify disputed peak-location totals before formal publication.

name: Red Barn
closureReason: Later ownership reduced advertising and allowed franchise agreements to expire.
history: Red Barn used distinctive barn-shaped buildings and operated in the United States, Canada, and Australia.
sourceNote: Peak count is commonly reported as a range of roughly 300 to 400 locations.

name: Pup 'N' Taco
closureReason: Taco Bell purchased most California locations and converted the properties.
history: The Southern California drive-in chain combined tacos, hot dogs, burgers, and pastrami on one menu.
sourceNote: The original California chain ended in 1984; related New Mexico operations continued under a modified name for a time.

name: Wetson's
closureReason: The regional chain struggled against larger national competitors and merged with Nathan's Famous.
history: Wetson's was a New York-area hamburger chain recognized by orange-circle branding and low-priced menu items.
sourceNote: The brand was discontinued after its mid-1970s merger and location closures.

name: Sandy's
closureReason: Hardee's acquired the company, and most restaurants converted to the Hardee's brand.
history: Sandy's Drive-In expanded across the Midwest before its restaurants were gradually rebranded.
sourceNote: The last location using the Sandy's brand is commonly reported as converting in 1979.

name: Gino's Hamburgers
closureReason: Marriott acquired the chain and converted many locations to Roy Rogers restaurants.
history: Gino's combined hamburger service with Kentucky Fried Chicken products and became a prominent Mid-Atlantic chain.
sourceNote: This record describes the original national chain, not later businesses using a similar revived name.

name: Carrols
closureReason: Most U.S. restaurants became Burger King locations; remaining European restaurants were later converted to Hesburger.
history: Carrols began as a hamburger chain, although the corporation later continued as a large Burger King franchise operator.
sourceNote: The restaurant brand disappeared, while the related corporation continued operating other restaurant brands.

name: White Tower Hamburgers
closureReason: The chain declined over many decades; the final Toledo restaurant closed after a fire.
history: White Tower used white fortress-style restaurant buildings and once operated in numerous U.S. cities.
sourceNote: Older summaries sometimes list 2004, but the final Toledo operation is reported to have remained until 2022.
